views.why: the owner's correction (2026-10-14, about 10:50): the ship plan's hull outline read as a rocket; his shuttle is a long flat wedge narrowing gradually to a sharp nose, with swept wings growing out of the body toward the back and the engines set into the flat stern. Redrawn after the overseer's check of plan v3 (2026-10-14): the first drawing gave the body a blunt front about 4.4 m wide behind the spike and front fins nearly the size of wings; this request says the body itself tapers to a sharp point and the front fins are small. Its outline and engines are traced from this view. The reference is his shuttle picture cropped out of its screenshot.
views.wording: The attached picture is a concept painting of a spaceship: a long, flat, wedge-shaped shuttle with off-white armour panels over a dark grey lower hull. Draw this exact same ship as a clean technical drawing on a plain white background, two orthographic views in one picture, both at the same scale with the nose pointing left: in the upper half, the ship seen from directly above (plan view); in the lower half, the same ship seen exactly from its side (side elevation), its nose and stern lined up with the view above. Keep its shape exactly as painted. Seen from above the body itself is a flat wedge, an arrowhead: its sides run in long straight lines that close gradually to a sharp point at the nose, with no blunt or square front anywhere; the nose spike is only a thin needle at that point. Near the nose there are only two small fins, much smaller than the wings, as small as in the painting. Toward the back, swept wings grow out of the body. The engines are set into the flat stern, flush with it, not sticking out. The round docking ring is on its side and the small angular windows are on its top deck. Flat even light, thin dark outlines, its own colours, no perspective, no shadows, no text, no labels, no dimensions, nothing else in the picture.

Draw one concept painting of another room inside the same spaceship, in exactly the same style, materials and light: dark grey panelled walls, orange padded and white painted panels, hexagonal door frames in orange and white panels, warm amber screens and readouts, white light strips. The room is the navigation room, about 2.8 m wide and 3 m long (ceiling 2.58 m at the front, 3.12 m at the back), seen from its doorway at standing eye height, the whole room in view. It holds: a star map table in the room's middle, glowing amber with a cyan route; two consoles along the front wall with a seat before them; two wall screens over the table: the route between the Moon and Mars; the door to the walkway in the ship's hexagonal frame; amber light strips at the wall tops, a white strip in the ceiling; grey panelled walls and ceiling, dark deck; a vent in the ceiling. No people, no text, no labels, nothing outside the room.
